questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really like the Australian nature and the animals, so I always knew that I wanted to go to Australia. Then I choose Sydney, because I thought it had more to offer than Melbourne - and it did!!! Also, in academic aspects I wanted to take courses that gave me a different perspective on international and global politics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I made amazing friends here because I was open to meet people. If you just have the right mindset, making friends is so easy even though it might seem scary.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Macquarie Universities website was challenging to navigate and it took time to figure out the units can them approved.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, just a general exchange study email that they inform you about. Most of the time, I had to push for them to answer my mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Be sure to get the special requisites in good time! because they are very slow with the process.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Even if you stay at MQ, live in the city! Dont live in Chatswood or Iglu residents. They charge way too much.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Search on flatmates or arrive to Sydney and go to in person viewings while you are here and maybe stay in an airbnb for the first 2 weeks.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In order to registrer for any class/unit you have to have a special waiver that allows you to take the unit, before you can even add it to your study plan. This process was so diffucult because it took several weeks to get any updates or information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did manage to get the classes I wanted, but I really pushed them for it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for special waivers as soon as possible.

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: MA

questions.answer:

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More active participation, more assignments during the semester rather than one final exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Terrorism - MA
Counter Terrorism in a Global and Australian context - MA
Australia's defence and strategic policy - MA
Europe and the World - MA

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As a student of Political Science, I thought these courses were interesting. Not very challenges given that I didnt know anything about Australia's defence policy or terrorism studies whatsoever. I managed, but I would encourages others to do more research into units that may align better with their studies. Also, Australia's defence and strategic policy was a final oral assessment which demanded too much i think.

questions.answer:
Coffee - best in the world, way cheaper than DK.
Food + social life in general - just expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: didnt really join any

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: didnt participate so i wouldnt now

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Coogee Pavillon! Do a weekend trip Melbourne and see the Great Ocean Road. Book a ticket to East or West Australia or NZ in the mid-semester break!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: so easy. Aussies are so kind and easy-going.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: no, unfortunantly not. All my friends were other international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing, other than Aussies wake up earlier and night life ends earlier than in DK.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nature! good coffee! amazing summer weather!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be aware of exam's form
2) Apply early for special waivers
3) Be prepared for a very diverse class of people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to travel so much and still finishing courses with decent marks (grades)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so social all the time, but it is so rewarding.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
